stem: A manufacturing study measures defect rate across 3 factorys, each containing multiple production lines. factory A has 5 observations with mean 69.4 % (within-factory SD = 9.5). factory B has 5 observations with mean 67.6 % (within-factory SD = 9.4). factory C has 20 observations with mean 69.6 % (within-factory SD = 6.5). The between-factory standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 5.8 and 14.5 %. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true defect rate for factory B, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-factory variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for factory B: 67.9 % (shrunk from raw 67.6). Range [67.7, 68.2] as between-factory SD varies from 5.8 to 14.5. Pooled mean: 69.2.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 69.2 % (weighted average of 3 factory means).
Shrinkage factor for factory B: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/5). At σ_between=9.7: B = 0.842.
Interval [67.7, 68.2] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (67.6) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (69.2) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
